install_overlay.guidance: Please don't use your keyboard or mouse. You can watch as KiWin works.
install_overlay.dry_run_complete: Dry run complete. No system changes were made.
install_overlay.complete_no_restart: Installation complete. KiWin will not restart your system automatically.

browser.title: Welcome. Please select your web browser.
browser.subtitle: KiWin will uninstall Microsoft Edge (You can turn it off, but it's not recommended). These are privacy-focused, secure browsers that you can use every day.

review.title: System is ready to debloat. Please review.
review.guidance:
The list on the left shows everything KiWin is going to do to your system. If there's something you don't want it to do, you can remove items from the list.

If everything looks good to you, select "Start."
review.no_internet_info: You aren't connected to internet. KiWin won't install a browser.
review.no_updates_warning: Update policy won't be configured. Updates may restore bloat and undo some of KiWin's settings.
review.nothing_to_do: Cannot start debloat process. Nothing to do.

advanced.title: Advanced settings
advanced.warning: Do not touch unless you know what you're doing!
advanced.winutil_tweaks_tooltip: One tweak name per line, e.g. WPFTweaksTelemetry. Applied by WinUtil during phase one.
advanced.undo_policy_done: Update policy removed. Windows will now receive full updates again.

remove_edge_permanently.tooltip: Uninstalls Microsoft Edge, and ensures it doesn't come back. You can always reinstall it yourself if you want. Apps that rely on it (msedgewebview2) will still work.

debloat_windows_phase_one.tooltip: KiWin utilizes ChrisTitusTech's WinUtil as part of its debloating process. The entire process is fully automated, so removing this step is not recommended.

debloat_windows_phase_two.tooltip: KiWin utilizes Raphire's Win11Debloat as part of its debloating process. The entire process is fully automated, so removing this step is not recommended.

configure_updates.tooltip: KiWin restricts Windows to security updates only, preventing bloatware from returning. This block is permanent on Pro and expires after 365 days on Home.

developer_mode.tooltip: When enabled, KiWin runs without showing the full-screen install overlay.

prevent_device_companion_apps.tooltip: Prevents additional software from being installed when plugging in devices (e.g. ads when plugging in a monitor). Poses potential security risk.

wpbt.tooltip: Prevents the WPBT firmware binary (a lower-level OEM mechanism) from running at boot. Some OEMs use it for legitimate purposes, but it can also be abused.

remove_onedrive.tooltip: Uninstalls OneDrive and disables its sync service. Your OneDrive files are kept, but the app is removed. Reinstalling later is possible.

remove_apps.tooltip: Removes bloatware apps such as Mail, People, Teams, Get Started, and more. Uninstalling is not reversible through KiWin, but apps can be reinstalled from the Microsoft Store.

remove_gaming_apps.tooltip: Removes the Xbox app, Game Bar and related gaming software. Turn this off if you play games on your PC.

helium.tooltip: Helium is a recommended browser—often compared to Brave, but acts more like LibreWolf for Chromium. It offers out-of-the-box privacy and uBlock Origin support without the bloat, though it lacks Sync and DRM.

firefox.tooltip: Firefox is not recommended out of the box, but with proper configuration, it is one of the best browsers—benefiting from rapid zero-day patches directly from Mozilla. Check out my custom setup: https://github.com/KabosuNeko/YuzuFox

waterfox.tooltip: Waterfox is recommended over Firefox out of the box as telemetry and tracking are pre-removed. However, zero-day patches are often delayed compared to upstream Firefox.

brave.tooltip: Brave is recommended with Chromium compatibility, Manifest V3, and built-in adblocking and fast zero-day patches. While notoriously bloated by default, KiWin automatically debloats it. If you're unsure which browser to choose, pick Brave.

librewolf.tooltip: LibreWolf is recommended for tech-savvy users wanting the best privacy and security here. While slightly too strict for everyday use, it receives zero-day patches faster than Waterfox (though behind stock Firefox ofc).
